Get variable from aeme

Source: R/get_var.R
get_var.Rd

Get variable from aeme

Usage

get_var(
  aeme,
  model,
  var_sim,
  depth = NULL,
  depth_ref = c("surface", "bottom"),
  return_df = TRUE,
  ens_n = 1,
  use_obs = FALSE,
  remove_spin_up = TRUE,
  cumulative = FALSE,
  zone = NULL,
  sed_layer = NULL
)

Arguments

aeme

Aeme object, or an AemeSummary. For a summary only model and var_sim apply, and the result has the surface and bottom series (layer) and every stat; filter output() for more control.

model

character vector; models to use. One or more of "dy_cd", "glm_aed", "gotm_wet", "simstrat_aed2". Defaults to all models if not found in aeme.

var_sim

character; variable in the AEME format (e.g. "HYD_temp").

depth

numeric; depth of the variable to extract, referenced to depth_ref. Default is NULL. If NULL, the variable profiles are extracted.

depth_ref

character; what depth is measured from when a single depth is extracted. "surface" (default): metres below the water surface. "bottom": metres above the lake bed, so depth = 1 is the water 1 m above the bottom. That is level - depth metres below the surface, with level the modelled water level (LKE_lvlwtr) on each date, so it follows the surface as the level rises and falls. On a date when the level is below depth (the point would be above the surface) the value is NA. Ignored when depth is NULL. (In AEME 0.4.0 and earlier "bottom" was measured from the basin's full depth, which only matches when the level equals that depth.)

return_df

logical; if TRUE, return a dataframe; if FALSE, return a list. Default is TRUE.

ens_n

integer; ensemble number to plot. Default is 1.

use_obs

logical; if TRUE, use observations to extract the variable at time and depth of observations. Default is FALSE. Use this option if you want to compare model output to observations. Observations recorded as a height above the lake bed (see add_obs()) are compared with the model profile at (the model's water level - that height) on each date, so they follow the model's own level rather than the depth they were placed at when added.

remove_spin_up

logical; remove spin-up period from plot. Default is TRUE.

cumulative

logical; if TRUE, return cumulative sum of variable

zone

integer; for GLM-AED sediment-zone variables (those with an nzones column, e.g. "SED_Fsed_oxy", "SED_temp"), keep only these sediment zones (GLM zone order, 1 = deepest). NULL (default) keeps all.

sed_layer

integer; for variables with a sediment-layer dimension ("SED_temp"), keep only these layers (1 = shallowest). NULL (default) keeps all. Sediment variables are returned in long format with one column per dimension (nzones, sed_layers); depth_ref/depth do not apply.

Value

If return_df = TRUE, a data frame with the same leading columns whether or not use_obs is used: Date, depth (NA for variables without a depth dimension), value, var_sim and Model. With use_obs = TRUE the column obs (the observation, paired with the model value) is added after value, plus depth_ref and height_above_bed when height-above-bed observations are present. Variables with non-standard dimensions (e.g. sediment zones) carry one column per extra dimension instead of depth. If return_df = FALSE, a list with one such data frame per model.
